paragraph: Westwood's single-family market is the whole story here, and it is a real seller's market. Twenty sales over six months at a median of $794,500, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.11, 90 percent of homes closing above asking, and a median of 10 days on market. Multiple offer situations are the norm, not the exception. The typical sale is a three-bedroom, two-bath colonial, with some split-levels and capes mixed in, and the range runs from $435,000 to $1,525,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Condos are a much smaller slice, five sales at a median of $381,000, mostly one-bedroom one-bath units, and they moved quickly too at 12 days. Five sales cannot carry a trend, so treat that tier as a price reference rather than a read on direction. On the monthly numbers, closings built into June and July and the last two months are printing medians at the high end of the six-month spread, which tracks the normal summer peak. If Westwood follows the usual arc, expect volume to taper modestly through fall. If you're deciding between tiers, it comes down to whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance, lower-price entry a condo gives you.
